text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: paging: p95 latency spike on /v1/stream (prod) - threshold 700ms, current ~1450ms. affected zones: us-east-2, eu-north-1. alert ref: ALRT-8420
Zoe (oncall): I'm looking. Hannah, any tickets from customers?
Hannah (support): three customers reported interactive stream stalls and occasional request resets starting ~22:03 UTC. collecting request ids now.
Priyanka (observability): baseline p50 ~75ms -> now ~210ms. p95 from ~260ms -> ~1450ms. onset at 22:02:37 UTC. adding trace samples.
Marco (infra): FYI we had a maintenance batch last night that updated kernel from 6.4.2 -> 6.4.3 on a subset of nodes in stream-pool-c at 01:15 UTC. I'll check which hosts landed the patch.
Lin (runtime): pulling traces for requests >800ms. query: traces where service=runtime and duration>800 order by duration desc. top examples show socket_write/epoll stalls; model_forward stable. sample span below:
```
SpanID: 0xb33c
operation: runtime.stream_handler
duration: 1487ms
  - read_prompts 10ms
  - model_forward 620ms
  - kv_lookup 7ms
  - net_send 840ms   <-- tail
```
Caleb (perf): can we run perf stat on an affected process? suggested counters: context-switches,cycles,instructions,cache-misses.
Marco (infra): running perf on node stream-12 (pid 41234):
```
perf stat -e context-switches,cycles,instructions,cache-misses -p 41234 -- sleep 4
  context-switches: 17290
  cycles: 8.02e+09
  instructions: 2.15e+09
  cache-misses: 9.9e+06
  cycles/instruction: 3.73  (baseline ~2.05)
```
Priyanka (observability): host metrics show increased futex wait times and epoll wake latency coinciding with the spike.
Lin (runtime): stack logs show `write() blocked 810ms` and threads reporting `futex_wait woke after 690ms`. example log:
```
[22:02:45] runtime[pid=41234]: write() blocked 812ms -> backtrace: __sys_write -> net_write -> epoll_wait
[22:02:45] runtime[pid=41240]: futex_wait woke after 692ms
```
Caleb (perf): cycles/instruction jump and higher voluntary context-switches indicate the CPU pipeline stalled or heavy kernel-level wake latency. matches a kernel-level scheduling/futex change.
Marco (infra): grepping kernel changelog: `commit d4e7 - futex: adjust wake ordering to mitigate thundering herd under heavy contention` landed in 6.4.3. that aligns with our timeline.
Zoe (oncall): mitigation options: 1) steer traffic away from stream-pool-c, 2) reduce per-worker thread concurrency to lower futex contention (runtime config), 3) rollback kernel on affected hosts. Which is fastest?
Lin (runtime): option 1 is the fastest and safest. option 2 requires a runtime configuration rollout which could take longer and may not fully restore tail latency. rollback is effective but slower.
Marco (infra): I'll apply routing override to prefer stream-pool-a/b and cordon stream-pool-c nodes for investigation. doing now.
Priyanka (observability): after routing change, p95 dropped from ~1450ms -> ~400ms within ~2 mins. p50 back to ~90ms. error traces reduced.
Hannah (support): notifying customers: mitigation applied and we're investigating root cause; will provide ETA for full remediation.
Lin (runtime): collecting full-span dumps and correlating request ids to server logs and perf output for RCA. hypothesis: futex/epoll wake-order change in 6.4.3 causes longer wake latency under our thread model -> socket writes block and p95 rises.
Caleb (perf): can we run a canary rollback to validate? Marco, can you provision one node with 6.4.2 and run the same synthetic load?
Marco (infra): provisioning canary now: stream-12-canary with 6.4.2. running synthetic: many concurrent small writes, high epoll churn. baseline vs canary: write latency median 12ms on canary vs 190ms on patched host under same load. perf on canary after load:
```
perf stat (canary):
  context-switches: 4800
  cycles: 3.95e+09
  instructions: 1.92e+09
  cycles/instruction: 2.05
```
Lin (runtime): trace for same request on canary shows net_send 14ms -> total ~650ms (model + net). good repro and clear improvement.
Caleb (perf): I'll add to RCA: perf snapshots, cycles/instruction comparison, futex/epoll tail latencies, and a small reproducer script.
Marco (infra): preparing rollback playbook if steering isn't sufficient. can do staged replacement back to 6.4.2 in low-traffic window.
Zoe (oncall): I'm going to step off for a short break; Marco you take lead. Lin continue capture and correlation. Priyanka keep dashboards updated. Hannah handle customer comms. Caleb assemble perf evidence for RCA.
Marco (infra): acknowledged. canary rollback validated; posting note to ops doc and scheduling replacement during 03:00 UTC window.
Priyanka (observability): creating host-level alert: cycles/instruction >2.8 OR avg futex_wait >150ms triggers an ops alert. adding ephemeral dashboard to track socket_write tail by host.
Hannah (support): sending update to impacted customers: mitigation applied (traffic steering), canary rollback shows improvement; full rollback planned during maintenance window.
Lin (runtime): saving span excerpts and logs to the RCA doc. snippet included here for timeline:
```
22:02:37 - first p95 jump detected
22:02:45 - multiple write() blocked >700ms logged
22:04:10 - routing override applied
22:06:30 - p95 returned to ~400ms
22:15:00 - canary rollback validated
```
Caleb (perf): recommended follow-ups for RCA: add perf-based guardrails, create a reproduce script to send to kernel maintainers, and evaluate runtime-level futex/backoff tuning as a mid-term mitigation.
Zoe (oncall): thanks team. We'll draft an RCA with timeline, perf evidence, span excerpts, mitigation steps, and owners. Who will write what?
Marco (infra): I'll own rollback runbook and AMI build.
Lin (runtime): I'll write the technical RCA section with traces and stack logs.
Priyanka (observability): I'll provide graphs and set up the new alerts.
Hannah (support): I'll draft customer-facing summary and update tickets.
Caleb (perf): I'll assemble perf snapshots and reproducer.
Zoe (oncall): perfect. incident state: mitigated (traffic steered), severity lowered to P2. leaving channel open for RCA draft and follow-ups.
IncidentBot: incident status updated -> mitigation active, follow-up ticket INC-2091 created for RCA and rollback tasks.
